subject: Staged acceptance milestones and latency offsets for Cerulean MAP
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cerulean.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staged acceptance milestones and latency offsets for Cerulean MAP

Samir —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Attached is an updated MAP (MAP_v2.xlsx) and a draft SLA (SLA_draft_REDWOOD.docx) that map our commercial milestones to measurable evaluation outcomes. High level:

- Objective: 90-day evaluation with two gated milestones (Pilot Acceptance, Production Ramp).
- Commercial anchoring: pricing tiers and a ramp commit tied to milestone completion.
- Latency SLOs and concessions: we can offer stepwise discounts and service credits tied to P95/P99 latency targets during the Pilot and Ramp windows.

The MAP sheet has a recommended calendar:
  1) Pilot (weeks 0–4): bench + integration, acceptance criteria: latency P95 <= 220ms, accuracy baseline test set >= 92%
  2) Pilot acceptance review (week 5): decision point — go/no-go for staged ramp
  3) Staged ramp (weeks 6–12): increase queries, target committed usage by week 12
  4) Final commercial close (week 13): full contract and discount tier applied

Proposed commercial trade-offs (short):
- If Cerulean signs a 12-month commit by week 13 at X qpm/month, we can offer a 10% volume discount and priority dedicated capacity.
- If we miss P99 latency > 1% of the time during the ramp window, Redwood will issue token-based credits equal to 5% of that month’s service fees for each incremental breach bracket (details in SLA draft).

I put conservative numbers in the capacity_plan.csv so you can validate forecasted GPU hours.

Questions for your team: what is your target committed qpm for month 3? Also please confirm whether you need any additional compliance artifacts for procurement.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if it helps.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: SLA_draft_REDWOOD.docx (document)]
[Attachment: capacity_plan.csv (csv)]

From: Samir Patel <samir@cerulean.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leah Gomez <leah.gomez@cerulean.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 May 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged acceptance milestones and latency offsets for Cerulean MAP

Ben, thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Commit sizing: our tentative target for month 3 is ~120M tokens/month (roughly correlates to the qpm numbers you gave). We need confidence that the dedicated pool can handle peak bursts without P99 spikes.
2) Credits: can you clarify the credit cadence — are credits monthly and automatic, or adjudicated per incident?
3) Regression tolerance: if model regression appears during ramp, do you propose rollback to a pinned model while we investigate, and would that affect the discount/credits?

Also attaching our internal eval timeline (Cerulean_Eval_Timeline.pdf) so you can see the dates we’re blocking internally. If you can send a short redlineable version of the SLA with explicit credit formulas we can share with procurement.

Samir
Samir Patel
VP Product, Cerulean AI
[Attachment: Cerulean_Eval_Timeline.pdf (pdf)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cerulean.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged acceptance milestones and latency offsets for Cerulean MAP

Samir —

Appreciate the timeline — aligns well. To answer your bullets directly and make the concessions concrete: 

1) Dedicated capacity and burst: we will reserve a dedicated pool sized for your 95th percentile expected qpm with autoscale headroom for short bursts. P99 spikes are what matter — our proposal is a 99th percentile SLO of <= 260ms during Pilot and <= 220ms during Ramp. If P99 breaches the agreed tiers, credits will be applied automatically to the monthly invoice per the SLA formula (not adjudicated). Exact credit tiers: 
  - Tier A: P99 breach rate 0.5%–1.0% => 2% service credit that month
  - Tier B: 1.0%–2.5% => 5% service credit that month
  - Tier C: >2.5% => 10% service credit + optional remediation plan

2) Credits cadence: automatic monthly adjustment applied as invoice line-item. We’ll include reporting access showing per-route latency percentiles so your SREs can validate.

3) Regression handling: we support model pinning/rollback to the prior verified model variant. Rollback pauses progress toward the next MAP milestone until regression is resolved. Pricing discounts tied to milestone completion will only apply once the milestone acceptance criteria are met with the pinned model.

Attached is an updated capacity_plan.csv with a small conservative buffer and example monthly credit calculations in the last tab. If this looks acceptable, Ben and I will prepare a redline of SLA_draft_REDWOOD.docx for your procurement.

Next steps: 1) confirm the month-3 commit (120M tokens = yes/no), 2) agree to the credit tiers above, 3) review the redline SLA when we send it (estimated EOD tomorrow).

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: capacity_plan.csv (csv)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cerulean.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 May 2027 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged acceptance milestones and latency offsets for Cerulean MAP

Looping in legal/finance next — one quick note from my side: the automatic crediting approach is fine but we’ll need Cerulean to accept the monitoring export clause (sharing per-route telemetry for verification) and a clause that limits aggregated credit liability to the monthly invoice (standard cap). Ben — can you send a DocuSign link when you have the redline? Otherwise this looks ready to proceed pending procurement review.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
